title: eval-harness: add per-prompt quality-gating CI hook + threshold config
author: Priya Menon
description: Motivation: add a per-prompt quality gating CI hook that fails the PR when configured prompt-sets regress beyond acceptable thresholds. This implements a CI-side enforcement for prompt-level metrics (exact-match, rouge, embedding-sim thresholds) so regressions are caught earlier and tied to PRs. Summary of changes: new CI hook and pipeline step; a small config schema for prompt-set gate thresholds; unit + integration tests; docs and example prompt-set config. Checklist: - [x] Implement hook and threshold config parsing - [x] Add unit tests for threshold logic - [x] Add integration test that runs a small regression suite - [x] Wire hook into eval-harness CI workflow with opt-in flag - [x] Add docs and example prompt-set config How it works: The new hook (eval_harness/ci/hooks/prompt_quality_gate.py) runs after eval jobs and compares current metrics to baselines stored in the repo (examples/prompt-sets/*.baseline.json). Gate config supports per-prompt thresholds and aggregate pass rates. CI behavior is opt-in by adding a pipeline matrix entry or setting EVAL_QUALITY_GATE=true in the workflow; default is off to avoid surprising large teams. Rollout plan: opt-in for a small set of internal repos for two weeks, then flip to opt-out for core runtime repos after monitoring for false positives. Backwards compatibility: default is a no-op unless customers add gate configs or CI flag. Testing: unit tests cover threshold parsing and edge cases, integration test runs the regression suite against a mocked evaluator, and e2e smoke is included in the workflow. Related: ENG-1428 (prompt regression CI), SUP-3412 (customer-reported prompt skew incident).
